text:
Sam: RFC — chunked blocktable + compact-rewrite for paged-attn KV cache. TL;DR: reduce fragmentation and cold-start OOMs by allocating blocktable entries in contiguous chunks, maintain per-chunk residency counters, and run a low-priority compaction/rewrite that coalesces sparse chunks. Handoff/evict stays lock-free on the hot path; compaction is background and uses epoch markers. Looking for feedback and volunteers for a prototype.

Sam: Problem summary: we've seen tail memory blowups and slower cold-starts when long-lived KV fragments are scattered across many small blocks. Current per-block alloc leads to high external fragmentation and many tiny free regions that the pager doesn't coalesce quickly.

Sam: Proposal (high level):
- allocate blocktable in "chunks" (e.g. 256 entries / chunk) instead of per-entry freelist
- track chunk meta: resident_count, gen, last_access_ts
- hot handoff remains per-entry CAS to avoid the hot-path lock penalty
- background compactor scans low-util chunks and rewrites live entries into denser chunks, then frees whole chunks back to OS/arena
- expose config flags: kv.chunked_alloc_v1, kv.compact_interval_ms, kv.chunk_size_entries

Sam: config example:```json
{"kv": {"chunked_alloc_v1": true, "chunk_size_entries": 256, "compact_interval_ms": 30000, "handoff_threshold_ms": 50}}
```

Priya: Nice. Do you have perf numbers? specifically p50/p99 latency impact for small token responses (1-4 tokens) and memory savings for steady-state long seq workloads?

Sam: Microbench results (local, opt builds):
- workload A (seq=512, batch=8, 8k steady clients): memory 90th -20%, 95th -18%, heap RSS -22%
- latency: p50 unchanged, p95 +1.6ms, p99 +3.2ms (mostly during compaction cycles)
- cold-start: startup RSS reduced ~28% on warmup phase (fewer fragmented pages)
- caveat: pathological micro-batch case (batch<4, very sparse KV reuse) showed small p99 regressions; we think can be mitigated by tweakable thresholds

Alex: How do we avoid races while compaction moves live entries? double-alloc/double-free risk if handoff touches an entry being moved. Also how to keep handoff lock-free?

Sam: Plan: per-chunk generation counter + per-entry owner pointer. Handoff does CAS on entry ptr; compactor marks chunk->gen++ to claim it then copies live entries into new chunk with new gen. Pseudocode:```c
// simplified
if (CAS(entry.ptr, old, MARKED_FOR_MOVE)) {
  // safe: entry will be ignored by consumer, compactor will finalize new ptr
}
// compactor sets chunk.gen = chunk.gen + 1 (atomic), writes new entries, then atomically swap chunk pointer in directory
```
This keeps per-entry CAS on hot path. Compaction will retry if CAS fails. We avoid global locks.

Maria: What's the interaction with pager eviction and our existing autoscale/cold-start heuristics? We don't want compactor triggering scale-up due to transient bursts of pagefaults. Also we should gate via runtime flag and do canaries.

Sam: Agreed. We'll gate behind kv.chunked_alloc_v1 flag. Compactor will run at very low priority and track compaction_pagefaults metric; if pagefaults spike above threshold, compactor backs off exponentially. Add telemetry: chunk_fill_ratio, compaction_cycles, handoff_retries, compaction_pagefaults.

perf-bot: CI perf run summary for branch chunked-blocktable (compare vs main):
- seq512 throughput: -0.4%
- p99 latency: +2.1ms (regression confined to periods where compaction runs)
- memory 90th: -20%
- regression observed with batch_size<4 and synthetic key-skew workload (link: https://ci.internal/perf/24876)

Priya: Thinking out loud: could we adapt chunk_size at runtime based on hot-key skew? If hotset small -> bigger chunks to reduce metadata; if scatter -> smaller chunks to speed compaction. Adaptive chunking + sample-driven resize maybe better than single static size.

Alex: I'll pick up allocator impl (ChunkDir + per-chunk meta + CAS handoff). Plan: prototype in sandbox, add unit tests for race cases, and run perf harness. ETA end of week.

Sam: Thanks Alex 🙏 Priya — can you own the perf harness runs and generate the canary configuration? Maria — can you own runtime gating + SLO rules for compactor backoff? I'll wire telemetry and the rewrite logic.

Maria: SGTM :thumbsup:. We'll do 2-week canary on a subset of Dedicated nodes, A/B traffic routes. If perf looks ok we'll promote.

infra-bot: NOTE: created perf job 2487654321-chunked-blocktable-canary; scheduled runs every 4h for the next 48h.

Sam: Updated RFC: adding adaptive chunk size note + telemetry list. I'll post follow-up with a minimal design doc and link to prototype code when Alex has a PR.

Alex: one more question — what's our target for compaction cpu budget? can we cap it to 5% token compute?

Sam: Yes we'll cap compaction to a soft 5% CPU budget per GPU host; extra cycles are only allowed during low-latency windows.
